- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to account for potential reversal or risk premium.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with upward bias starting from day of sentiment pivot.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is bullish, then underestimates later (8–30) when sentiment turns neutral or bearish — adjust with lagged sentiment smoothing.
